correctness.rationale: The renewal reward martingale variance rate is v=[(1-m^2)A+m^2B]/E N with A=E R^2 and B=E(R-rho N)^2; this handles correlated R,N within each iid cycle. Direction-sign reversal KL per cycle is 2m atanh(m), hence Q proportional m/[(1-(1-b)m^2)atanh(m)]. Differentiating reduces sign to 1-b-g(m), where g=(1-t)/(m^2(1+t)), t=(1-m^2)atanh(m)/m. Positive integral representations prove g strictly increases from 1/3 to 1, yielding exactly the global three-regime classification and endpoints, no finite-grid inference. New independent numerical grid tests checked 300 derivative signs, 999 monotonicity pairs and the unique root/gain at b=.2. Efficiency is mathematical KL information cost only, not necessarily physical entropy production.

value.rationale: Whether finite directional drive improves precision per binary selection-information cost is a natural bias-control question. A universal b=B/A condition separating interior optimum from weak-bias operation is a precise nontrivial operationally meaningful boundary, while avoiding unsupported device-independent thermodynamic claims.

final_claim: For bounded iid renewal cycle rewards R>=0 and integer durations N>=1, with independent Bernoulli direction bias m and fixed cycle law, the defined KL-reversal-cost current efficiency has a unique nonzero-bias optimum iff 0<B/A<2/3, a weak-bias supremum if B/A>=2/3, and a strong-bias divergence if B=0.
